chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

A messenger from God came to me and said: 'Indeed, God the Exalted and Mighty commands you to recite the Quran in one letter.' I said: 'O Lord, be lenient with my nation.' He said: 'Indeed, God the Exalted and Mighty commands you to recite the Quran in one letter.' I said: 'O Lord, be lenient with my nation.' He said: 'Indeed, God commands you to recite the Quran in seven letters.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Quran being revealed in seven letters (ahruf)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal elucidates the theological basis for the seven ahruf (modes) of Quranic recitation, illustrating the divine concession (rukhsah) granted to the Prophet Muhammad to accommodate the linguistic diversity of early Arab tribes. It highlights the progression from a single, rigorous mode to seven, emphasizing the Quran's adaptability and ease of memorization, a concept central to Shia and Sunni jurisprudence regarding qira'at. The narrative underscores the mercy inherent in the revelation, ensuring the text remained accessible without compromising its integrity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-45 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hilal , on the authority of Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“Gabriel was sent to me by the Honorable the Exalted God and told me, ’God has ordained that you recite the Quran in one letter only.’ I said, ‘O God! Please be more lenient with my nation.’ Then Gabriel said, ‘The Honorable the Exalted God ordained that you recite the Quran in seven letters.’”
